+---
+## What
+Prove the web verbs through the JavaScript sandbox, with no network. Design: `web.md` § "Goal" (the snippet) and the `WebRunCodeTests` row of § "Testing / Level 1".
+
+- Create `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/Fixtures/WebRunFixtures.swift`, modelled on `Fixtures/FilesRunFixtures.swift`: make a `MultiTool` with `.withWeb(configuration:sessionConfiguration:)`, where the session configuration uses `WebStubURLProtocol` and the configuration uses literal test keys; add a `runSnippet` helper.
+- Create `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/WebRunCodeTests.swift`, modelled on `FilesCrossOpFlowTests.swift`.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] The snippet of `web.md` § "Goal" runs over stubbed Brave and page responses and returns three pages with titles and content heads.
+- [ ] `Promise.all` over three `tools.web.fetch` calls returns three results.
+- [ ] A guard refusal and a bad argument reach the snippet as a value with `correction`, not as a thrown exception.
+- [ ] A keyed provider configured with the literal key `test-secret-123` answers the search, and the text `test-secret-123` is in no return value and no console output of any snippet.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] The file above, with one test for each criterion.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter WebRunCodeTests`. All pass. Then run `swift test`.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #web
\ No newline at end of file

 assignees:

+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m3cmx2nr90gy8mp2ms4dgren
+  text: |-
+    Research:
+    - `withWeb(configuration:sessionConfiguration:)` makes `WebCapability`, which makes `WebContext` with `SystemHostResolver`. There is no resolver seam on this path.
+    - The Brave HTML host (`search.brave.com`) and the Brave API host (`api.search.brave.com`) are guarded requests. The guard calls the resolver for each name host. Thus through `withWeb` alone, a search does a real DNS lookup. Only SearXNG (host configuration) is not guarded, and only literal IP hosts skip the resolver.
+    - Decision: add an internal seam. `WebCapability` gets an internal `init(configuration:sessionConfiguration:resolver:)`. `MultiTool.Builder` gets an internal `withWeb(configuration:sessionConfiguration:resolver:)` that holds the replace logic. The public forms forward with `SystemHostResolver()`. The public API does not change. `HostResolver` is internal, thus a public parameter is not possible.
+    - `MultiToolBuilder.swift` is 461 lines before this change (more than 400). `source` is `private`, thus the web overload cannot move to an extension file without a change of access.
+    - Console output of a snippet is in the rendered `MultiTool.call` output (see `ToolReturnLedgerTests`). Thus one string check covers the return value and the console.
+    - Existing tests use top-level fixture functions (`FilesRunFixtures`). The swift `immutability` rule says a function belongs to a type, thus the new fixture uses a struct.
